requirements.title: Actual arguments correspond to dummy arguments by keyword or reduced-list position
requirements.definition: A procedure reference actual argument list establishes actual-to-dummy correspondence by argument keyword or by position in the reduced dummy argument list. The reduced list omits a passed-object dummy argument. One actual argument corresponds to each nonoptional dummy argument, at most one actual corresponds to each optional dummy argument, and every actual corresponds to a dummy argument.

pending.keyword-correspondence: Call an explicit-interface subroutine with a=11 and b=17 supplied by reversed keywords into caller sentinels -71 and -72; expect dummy a receives 11 and dummy b receives 17. Mutant removes keywords so the swapped positional values are observed.
pending.positional-correspondence: Call the same subroutine positionally with distinct values 23 and 29; initialize result sentinels to -81 and -82 and expect first dummy 23 and second dummy 29.
pending.passed-object-reduced-list: Invoke type-bound procedure obj%set(41) whose passed-object dummy stores 41 in obj%slot initialized to -5; pass a second ordinary dummy initialized to -6 to prove the data-ref supplied the omitted passed-object position.
pending.nonoptional-exactly-one-correspondence: Source-control negative omits required dummy b from an explicit-interface call; positive control supplies b=2 and records both assignments. This unnumbered program restriction has no required diagnostic claim.
pending.optional-at-most-one-correspondence: Source-control negative supplies optional dummy opt twice, once positionally and once by keyword; positive control supplies opt once and observes PRESENT(opt) plus value 19.
pending.every-actual-has-dummy: Source-control negative supplies an extra positional actual to a one-dummy procedure; positive control has one actual and observes dummy value 31.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish distinguished non-default state first, then observe portable single-image properties such as exact integer values, exact character values, PRESENT status, defined pointer-association inquiries, rank and bound inquiry results, and caller-side sentinels after procedure return. Unnumbered program restrictions do not create a required processor diagnostic; negative examples for those facets are source-control material only.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Diagnostics are not claimed unless a numbered constraint or syntax rule requires them. Undefined association status, undefined definition status, processor-dependent argument-passing mechanisms, storage addresses, descriptor layouts, and coarray/image behavior are not executable oracles here.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 13 for source form, type compatibility, declaration attributes, designators, array element order, expressions, execution constructs, data transfer, and formatting foundations already present in this suite. Unregistered dependencies retained for future fixtures: later clause 15 optional, pointer, allocatable, procedure, elemental, generic, pure/simple, sequence association, and finalization rules; clause 16 inquiry intrinsics and ISO_FORTRAN_ENV support; clauses 14, 17, 18, and 19 for modules, IEEE support, C interoperability, and association/lifetime state.

accounting.rationale: The note gives an example invocation and is not normative.

Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; C1546-C1549 had no existing tests and carry one-feature diagnostic plans, and sequence association is observed through element order in both directions. Source accounting only.
